content.text: {"title":"The Pond Concert and the Listener in the Reeds","premise":"At sunset, Mina and Jojo help Pip the frog prepare a concert on a lily-pad stage. Pip wants a grand croaking finale, Mina wants a shy neighbor to feel welcome, and Jojo wants to win the ridiculous Golden Pebble prize. The pond’s listeners, floating props, and a mistaken belief about a quiet neighbor change what kind of concert can succeed.","cast_and_props":"Characters: Pip (frog performer; wants applause and a proper croak), Mina (child; wants neighbor Nella to join the party), Jojo (child; wants the Golden Pebble prize and believes louder is better), and Nella (quiet snail neighbor; wants to listen privately, then possibly participate). Props: lily-pad stage, reed-bell garland, floating pebble microphone, Golden Pebble prize, and a paper invitation. Shared setting: one pond shore and its nearby reeds. State slots include each character’s location, wants or beliefs, the invitation’s delivery, prop owners/locations, concert style, performance completion, and audience response.","kernels_and_interactions":"1. Invitation/knowledge: Mina observes or tells Jojo that Nella is nearby; delivering the invitation changes whether Nella attends. 2. Ownership and trade: Jojo may give the floating pebble microphone to Pip, or Pip may trade the Golden Pebble for Nella’s tiny shell chime. 3. Preparation/performance: placing the reed bells and choosing a quiet, splashy, or echoing style enables a completed concert. 4. Mistaken belief: Jojo initially believes Nella dislikes music; observing Nella’s hidden listening spot reveals she dislikes sudden loud sounds, not songs. 5. Audience response: Nella’s response, pond applause, or prize presentation becomes a real final outcome. These kernels share the same invitation, microphone, reed bells, and final performance scenes across routes.","seed_parameters":"Use the seed to vary initial physical/social conditions: (A) Jojo owns the floating microphone and Nella’s invitation is undelivered; (B) a breeze has scattered the reed-bell garland while Nella is already listening unseen; (C) Pip has promised a booming finale, but the only visible listener is Nella’s empty-looking reed nook and Jojo believes she has gone away; (D) Nella has sent a shell chime as a possible gift, but Jojo thinks it is a prize token. Initial premise keys: microphone.owner, bells.location, invitation.delivered, jojo.knows.nella.likes_music, and shell_chime.owner. Outcomes must vary: concert.style, n​ella.attended, n​ella.response, prize.owner, and performance.completed.","candidate_scenes":"1 observe_nella_nook: Mina notices the reed nook or hears a shell chime; enables the right invitation or style choice. 2 tell_jojo_about_nella: Mina shares what she learned; Jojo’s mistaken belief can change. 3 deliver_invitation: Mina carries the paper invitation to Nella. 4 find_scattered_bells: the children gather the reed bells. 5 lend_microphone: Jojo gives the floating pebble microphone to Pip. 6 trade_prize_for_chime: Pip offers the Golden Pebble for Nella’s shell chime. 7 place_bells: the garland is hung on reeds. 8 promise_quiet_song: Pip changes from booming to gentle. 9 promise_splash_song: Pip keeps the noisy style when Nella is absent or the pond crowd wants excitement. 10 welcome_nella: Nella accepts the invitation or emerges from hiding. 11 perform_quiet_concert: Pip and the children complete a soft concert; Nella responds warmly. 12 perform_splash_concert: Pip completes a grand noisy concert; the pond crowd responds and Jojo may win the prize. 13 perform_shell_concert: Nella joins with the shell chime; the audience response and prize ownership differ. Reuse observation, invitation, bell placement, microphone lending, and final performance scaffolding across all paths. Mark only promise_quiet_song and welcome_nella as pivotal.","constraints":"Build 12–18 candidates, 5–10 selected events, and 3–5 kernel families. Every scene needs guards for knowledge, ownership, location, and motive where relevant. The inciting action must establish the actual seed problem before any response. The goal must require performance.completed plus a real audience response. No route should merely select a concert style. Keep all state scalar and declare every slot first; use observe, tell, and transfer where they enable later actions. Supply conditional prose for each initial problem, each discovery, and each materially different ending.","different_endings":"Quiet welcome: Nella attends, joins with the shell chime, and the final image is tiny ripples carrying a soft rhythm beneath the loud pond. Splashy triumph: Pip performs the booming concert, the pond crowd cheers, and Jojo receives the Golden Pebble while the microphone bobs like a silver duck. Shared prize: Nella responds warmly after the children alter the concert, and the Golden Pebble is placed beside her shell chime as both children and frog bow. Private discovery: Nella listens from the reeds and responds without entering, leaving the final image of a shell chime swinging gently where nobody expected an audience."}
